notes: Twenty lists read, 105 entries. oecd.org returned 403 (How's Life chapter), so OECD entries are the Health dimension from the OECD slide deck on unstats.un.org, the Better Life Index health indicators from Wikipedia, and deaths of despair from a healthpopuli summary of How's Life 2024. The Ipsos Health Service Report 2025 PDF gave two ranked lists (health problems; health-system problems) with 30-country averages; its text was extracted with a small zlib script because WebFetch could not read the PDF. The Gallup MIP page loaded without its table, so only the Healthcare category (named in the money sweep) is listed. The national 211 snapshot names only mental health and substance use among health needs; Michigan, New Jersey and Ontario 211 reports failed to load or parse. medicine-shortages stays a draft: ASHP's statistics page returned 403. Overlaps for refine: drug-prices and no-health-insurance are narrower than one-illness-away (Medical bills); short-staffed-care, hospital-closing and care-quality are societal views of cant-get-care (personal Healthcare); dementia overlaps caregiving and older-people-alone; obesity overlaps eating-badly; pregnancy-care overlaps womens-health only by topic. Wikidata QIDs from the wbsearchentities API (30 lookups, rate-limited, not counted as searches). insurance-denials was withdrawn because the body sweep 20261019-224657 proposes the same pain under that ID; its evidence, for that candidate: KFF (https://www.kff.org/affordable-care-act/consumer-survey-highlights-problems-with-denied-health-insurance-claims/, accessed 2026-10-19): "18% of insured adults say they experienced denied claims in the past year." and "roughly 6 in 10 insured adults experience problems when they use their insurance." road-deaths was withdrawn because the safety sweep 20261019-230042 proposes the same pain under that ID; its evidence, for that candidate: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/road-traffic-injuries (accessed 2026-10-19): "Approximately 1.16 million people die each year as a result of road traffic crashes."; https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/road-traffic-injuries (accessed 2026-10-19): "Road traffic injuries are the leading cause of death for children and young adults aged 5–29 years."
